purpose: Classify registered co-ownership interests and route questions about joint tenancy, tenancy in common, severance, transfer and survivorship without inferring beneficial ownership from the register alone.
legal_distinctions: Joint tenancy and tenancy in common are distinct forms of co-ownership.
Registered proprietorship does not necessarily resolve every beneficial or trust interest.
Survivorship and succession are distinct legal events and must be analysed with the applicable ownership form.
Severance can alter the co-ownership relationship and requires evidence of the relevant legal event.
A court order concerning sale or partition is distinct from the resulting registration steps.
Mortgages, burdens and other registered interests remain separate layers.
evidence_requirements: death certificate and succession documentation where relevant
trust documentation where a beneficial interest is alleged
official_routes: Tailte Éireann Land Registry registration services
Tailte Éireann forms and registration rules
Probate and succession routes where a co-owner has died
Courts Service where judicial partition or sale is relevant
guardrails: Never infer beneficial ownership solely from registered names.
Never assume survivorship without establishing the relevant co-ownership form and legal event.
Never treat a death as automatically resolving every title or beneficial-interest issue.
Never infer severance without supporting evidence.
Never collapse legal title and beneficial ownership into one concept.
